rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for the resentful feeling of wanting what someone else has.

example.english: I feel a bit of envy when I see other people getting promoted and getting a raise.
example.traditional: 我見到人哋升職加人工，真係有啲妒忌心。
example.jyutping: ngo5 gin3 dou3 jan4 dei6 sing1 zik1 gaa1 jan4 gung1 zan1 hai6 jau5 di1 dou3 gei6 sam1

rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for feeling envious of someone’s good fortune or possessions.

example.english: I really envy them for getting a new car so quickly.
example.traditional: 我真係眼紅佢咁快買到新車。
example.jyutping: ngo5 zan1 hai6 ngaan5 hung4 keoi5 gam3 faai3 maai5 dou2 san1 ce1

rows.note: Use this for the more explicit or somewhat formal expression of envy, especially when stressing resentment toward the person.

example.english: They openly expressed envy of the other person's achievements.
example.traditional: 佢公開表示妒忌對方嘅成就。
example.jyutping: keoi5 gung1 hoi1 biu2 si6 dou3 gei6 deoi3 fong1 ge3 sing4 zau6

rows.jyutping: ling6 jan4 ngaan5 hung4 ge3 N
rows.note: Use this pattern when a person or thing is being described as an object that others envy.

example.english: Their salary is truly the kind of salary people envy.
example.traditional: 佢份人工真係令人眼紅嘅人工。
example.jyutping: keoi5 fan6 jan4 gung1 zan1 hai6 ling6 jan4 ngaan5 hung4 ge3 jan4 gung1
